title: Shop-grade vehicle, job history, and configuration foundation
scope: Add a durable, versioned Vehicle Record and configuration-history foundation around the existing local-first CarbTune workflow, migrate legacy jobs idempotently, prove one vehicle can retain multiple immutable historical jobs, and prepare explicit technician/audit attribution without authentication or a backend.
objectives: Persist stable Vehicle Records separately from jobs while keeping chassis and installed-engine identity independent.
Support multiple historical jobs per vehicle and start a new job from an existing vehicle without mutating old jobs.
Preserve versioned configuration snapshots, job outcome history, validation lifecycle truth, technician attribution, and audit relationships.
Migrate existing localStorage jobs safely and idempotently without inventing unknown facts.
Integrate fast shop-oriented vehicle selection and history into the existing technician workflow.
Validate, document, commit, push, and observe CI/deployment through the protected CT-0058 workflow.
constraints: No PostgreSQL deployment, fake backend, authentication system, broad frontend rewrite, or competing service model.
Preserve all existing saved-job compatibility, duplicate/delete safeguards, technician workflow, and CT-0059 validation lifecycle rules.
Prefer archive and append-only history; never fabricate missing vehicle, component, actor, or verification facts.
Use only the repository-scoped CT-0058 permission configuration and protected Git wrapper.
implementationNotes: CT-0058 anomaly observed before application changes: protected wrapper pull was denied access to .git/FETCH_HEAD inside the restricted sandbox; the same narrow wrapper command succeeded after explicit escalation. This operation should have been covered by CT-0058 and may warrant a repository-scoped policy correction, not a machine-wide grant.
